How MISO Supports Large Energy Demand
              While Protecting Reliability




Large energy users — like a data centers — often seek to
connect to the grid faster than new infrastructure can be
built. And because they consume so much energy, the grid
needs more generation and transmission infrastructure.

MISO’s challenge is to support the reliable connection of
large loads to the grid through efficient studies, flexible
service options, clear reliability requirements and greater
transparency about who pays for grid upgrades.


MISO’S RESPONSE
MISO has already collaborated with utilities, states, data center owners, environmental groups and other stakeholders
to establish a framework that enables large loads. Recently, in response to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s
(FERC) Large Load Show Cause Order, MISO developed proposals that build on established planning processes and
stakeholder input.

MISO’s proposals address regional transmission planning, service and reliability. They also address affordability by providing
states and utilities with tools and flexibility to help protect existing customers as demand grows. At the same time, MISO’s
framework preserves the traditional roles of federal and state regulators, with FERC overseeing wholesale rates and states
retaining authority over retail rates, siting and economic development decisions.

WHAT MISO IS PROPOSING
MISO’s filings are intentionally focused on FERC’s direction in the Show Cause Order. Components addressing cost-shifting
were filed jointly with transmission owners.

                                              remain within state jurisdiction.



WHAT HAPPENS NEXT

FERC is reviewing MISO’s filings and determining whether the proposed Tariff changes are just and reasonable. Timely
approval of proposals is critical to help keep pace with unprecedented large-load growth and ensure the infrastructure
needed to serve that demand can be planned and deployed efficiently. MISO will address any required proposal
modifications and work on implementation plans for Q1 2027.
